messages:
alex: Quick RFC follow-up — lazy page reclamation coordinator prototype.

alex: TL;DR: only reclaim host-backed pages when the residency delta exceeds a hysteresis window AND local pending-allocs > reclaim_threshold. sketch: https://redwood.internal/rfc/coords (wip)

maria: Clarify: how does this interact with our KV cache? we must avoid evicting pages that are hot in the cache.

alex: Plan: coordinator reads per-region cache_pin bitset (set by serving runtime). If cache_pin==1 skip reclamation for that region. Fast-path: prefix cache entries pinned in LRU hotlist.

chris: Cross-node concern: reclamation spikes can cause remote pulls / migration storms. Propose per-NUMA reclaim_budget + backoff decay to smooth it.

alex: Yeah — per-node budget + global backpressure. budget = max(1, floor(local_free * budget_pct)). Also rate-limit remote migration ops per-second.

jordan: Observability request: expose counters: reclaimed_pages, skipped_cache_pins, remote_migrations, reclaim_cycles, last_budget_size. Add tracing/span on coordinator decisions.

alex: I'll add an experiment plan: synthetic seq-len 1024 load, 50% cached prefixes, vary budget_pct 0.02/0.05/0.1. Hypothesis: p99 tail improves 8-12% at 0.05 with modest cost. Will push patch and perf table.

ci-bot: build passed for branch lazy-page-coord. tests: mem-reclaim.* ok :white_check_mark:

maria: SGTM — please add a short doc in eng-runtime/notes about the cache_pin contract so private deployments can opt out.

alex: Will do. Thanks all :thumbsup:
